req.title: PUT /players/{id} requires body
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 422 when PUT /players/{playerId} is called without a request body.

doc.reasoning: R-PLAYER-038 states that PUT /players/{playerId} must return HTTP 422 when called without a request body. The actual endpoint in the source is PUT /players/squadnumber/{squad_number}. Three test cases are designed: (1) NEG — send PUT with no body at all to a known squad number, expect 422; (2) EP positive — send PUT with a valid body to a known squad number, expect 204 (confirms the 422 is body-absence-specific, not a blanket failure); (3) BVA — send PUT with an empty JSON object {} (body present but all required fields missing), expect 422, distinguishing 'no body' from 'empty body' at the boundary of body presence. Together these kill status-code constant mutations (422->400, 422->200), boolean-body-required mutations, and operator-flip mutations on the body-presence check.

preconditions: Database is pre-loaded with 26 player rows
Squad number 10 exists: Kabir Mary Reddy, Right Winger, DM, River Plate, Ligue 1
actions: Send PUT /players/squadnumber/10 with a fully valid PlayerRequestModel JSON body matching squad_number=10
expected: Status code is exactly 204, confirming 422 is body-absence-specific

tests.executable:
from main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
import json

client = TestClient(app, raise_server_exceptions=False)

def test_put_player_valid_body_returns_204():
    payload = {
        "firstName": "Kabir",
        "middleName": "Mary",
        "lastName": "Reddy",
        "dateOfBirth": "1910-01-01T00:00:00.000Z",
        "squadNumber": 10,
        "position": "Right Winger",
        "abbrPosition": "DM",
        "team": "River Plate",
        "league": "Ligue 1",
        "starting11": False
    }
    response = client.put(
        "/players/squadnumber/10",
        content=json.dumps(payload),
        headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"}
    )
    assert response.status_code == 204

test_put_player_valid_body_returns_204()

from main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

client = TestClient(app, raise_server_exceptions=False)

def test_put_player_no_body_status_not_200_or_204():
    response = client.put("/players/squadnumber/1")
    assert response.status_code == 422
    assert response.status_code != 200
    assert response.status_code != 204
    assert response.status_code != 400
    assert response.status_code != 404
    body = response.json()
    assert "detail" in body

tests.name: test_put_player_partial_body_missing_required_fields_returns_422
preconditions: Database is pre-loaded with 26 player rows
Squad number 5 exists in the database
actions: Send PUT /players/squadnumber/5 with a body containing only optional fields (no required first_name, last_name, position, squad_number)
expected: Response body contains 'detail' key with validation errors
trace: R-PLAYER-038: BVA boundary — body present but incomplete; required fields absent triggers same 422 as no-body; catches mutations that only check body presence vs field validation
tests.executable:
from main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
import json

client = TestClient(app, raise_server_exceptions=False)

def test_put_player_partial_body_missing_required_fields_returns_422():
    payload = {
        "middleName": "Karan",
        "dateOfBirth": "1905-01-01T00:00:00.000Z",
        "team": "Independiente",
        "league": "Liga Profesional",
        "starting11": False
    }
    response = client.put(
        "/players/squadnumber/5",
        content=json.dumps(payload),
        headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"}
    )
    assert response.status_code == 422
    body = response.json()
    assert "detail" in body
    assert isinstance(body["detail"], list)
    assert len(body["detail"]) > 0

test_put_player_partial_body_missing_required_fields_returns_422()
